gemini.overview: The Galápagos Islands are known for stark volcanic coasts and dramatic rock formations rising from the Pacific. The signature view is Pinnacle Rock on Bartolomé Island, a jagged volcanic cone flanked by beaches. Beyond the famous sights, the archipelago is made up of quiet bays, rugged shorelines, and lava fields.

blurbs.text: Warm, sunny weather and clear blue skies show the dark lava fields, white sand beaches and Pinnacle Rock against the ocean.
A low gray mist called the garúa often hangs over the highlands and the coasts, softening the colors of the lava fields and the beaches, though clear spells still show Pinnacle Rock.

gemini.depth_why: Scores rise in the dry season when visibility is best and fall slightly in the wet season.
gemini.overview: The Great Barrier Reef is one of the world's premier coastal landscapes, defined by its vast network of coral cays, turquoise waters, and white sand beaches. The signature views are seen from the water or the air, where the scale of the reef systems becomes clear. Whitehaven Beach is a major draw for its swirling silica sands and clear shallows. The scenery is best viewed during the dry season, when the water is clearest and the skies are mostly sunny.

blurbs.text: The wet season brings heavy rains, higher humidity, and occasional cyclones. Cloud cover and runoff can reduce water clarity, making the reef colors less vibrant from the air and the water.
The rains are lighter and the skies are mostly clear. Water visibility is excellent, giving views of the coral formations and the swirling sands of Whitehaven Beach.

The dry season offers the clearest skies and the best water visibility. The contrast between the deep blue ocean, the turquoise shallows, and the bright coral cays is at its sharpest, making this the best time for scenic flights and boat trips.
Humidity and temperatures are climbing toward the wet season. The views remain strong, though afternoon clouds and early rains can soften the light on the water.

gemini.depth_why: Visibility and access change with the Harmattan dust and the rainy seasons.
gemini.overview: Ghana is known for its palm-fringed Atlantic coastline and dense tropical forests. Visitors can walk above the jungle canopy at Kakum National Park, look out over the ocean from the coastal forts of Cape Coast, and hike to Wli Waterfalls in the eastern highlands. The views are clearest and most accessible in fall, just after the rainy season.

blurbs.text: Harmattan winds blow in fine dust from the north, creating a haze that obscures long-distance views along the coast and in the eastern highlands.
The air is free of the seasonal dust, giving sharp views of the coastline and the forest canopy ahead of the heaviest rains.
Heavy seasonal rains swell the rivers and waterfalls, but frequent downpours and muddy unpaved roads complicate access to remote forest trails.
The landscape is lush and green from the recent rains, and clear skies provide sharp visibility for photographing the coast and hiking to the waterfalls.

gemini.depth_why: Scores rise and fall with the opening and closing of the high-elevation roads.
gemini.overview: The region is known for steep, glacially carved peaks with glaciers still tucked into the high basins. The Going-to-the-Sun Road crosses the Continental Divide at Logan Pass, providing access to high alpine viewpoints. Lower elevations feature dense forests and large, reflective bodies of water like Lake McDonald.

blurbs.text: Heavy snow shuts most routes, including the higher elevations of the Going-to-the-Sun Road. Views are limited to the lower valleys and the frozen edges of Lake McDonald.
Lower elevations and valley roads open as the snowpack begins to melt. Waterfalls run high, though Logan Pass remains blocked by snow.
Access improves significantly as plows clear the higher roads. Snowmelt fuels heavy flows in the rivers and waterfalls, and the lower lakes reflect the surrounding peaks.
The Going-to-the-Sun Road is open, allowing drives over Logan Pass. The high alpine scenery, deep glacial valleys, and clear waters of Lake McDonald are all in view.
Autumn brings yellow larch needles to the forests. Snow begins to fall at higher elevations, often closing Logan Pass and limiting access to the alpine viewpoints by the end of the month.

gemini.depth_why: Scores rise through spring to a lush summer and a sharp October peak for fall colors, then drop as trees bare and high roads close for winter.
gemini.overview: Great Smoky Mountains National Park is known for its dense, mist-covered forests and rolling mountain ridges. Visitors drive or hike to viewpoints like Clingmans Dome and the open valley of Cades Cove, passing streams and waterfalls along the way. The scenery peaks in October when the hardwood forests turn bright orange, red, and yellow.

blurbs.text: Trees are bare, opening up views through the forest that are hidden in summer. The road to Clingmans Dome is closed for the winter, limiting access to the highest viewpoint.
Spring brings fresh green foliage across the lower and middle slopes. Streams and waterfalls run high from spring rain.
The mountains are covered in a thick, unbroken canopy of green. Morning fog often settles in the valleys, creating the smoky look the park is named for.
Fall foliage transforms the mountainsides into bright patches of red, orange, and yellow. The color usually starts at the highest elevations early in the month and moves down into the valleys.
Most leaves have fallen by the middle of the month, leaving a carpet of brown on the forest floor. The bare branches reveal the underlying ridges and valleys.

gemini.depth_why: Scores rise from closed winter months to a summer peak when ice and fjords are accessible.
gemini.overview: Greenland is known for its massive ice cap, deep fjords, and coastal mountains. The Ilulissat Icefjord is the most famous sight, where enormous icebergs calve into the sea. South Greenland offers a mix of green valleys, jagged peaks, and glaciers reaching the water. The best views come from boats and small planes.

blurbs.text: Deep winter brings extreme cold, heavy snow, and polar darkness. Most boat tours and flights for sightseeing are suspended, and the landscape is largely inaccessible.
Daylight is returning and the sea ice is breaking up in places. Few boat tours run yet, and most areas are still locked in ice and snow.
The sea ice is breaking up, and some boat tours are running, though many areas are still locked in ice and snow.
The midnight sun provides endless daylight for viewing the icebergs and fjords. The Ilulissat Icefjord can be seen by boat, and the coastal mountains are clear of snow for hiking.
Days shorten quickly and temperatures drop. The first snows dust the mountains, and boat tours still run in September.
Short days and falling temperatures make access difficult by late October, and fresh snow covers the mountains.

gemini.depth_why: Visibility and road access change with the dry and wet seasons.
gemini.overview: Lake Atitlán sits in a massive caldera surrounded by three steep volcanoes, forming the country's most recognized landscape. The colonial streets of Antigua share a similar volcanic backdrop, with Agua, Fuego, and Acatenango rising directly above the city. The northern region shifts to dense jungle, where the turquoise limestone pools of Semuc Champey step down a forested river and the temple tops of Tikal rise above the canopy.

blurbs.text: Clear skies provide the sharpest outlines of the volcanoes and the lake.
Agricultural fires and rising humidity create a thick haze that often obscures distant peaks.
Heavy rains and low clouds frequently hide the mountains and can cause mudslides on rural routes.
The rains end, leaving the highland forests green and the air clear for long-distance visibility.

gemini.depth_why: Scores rise through spring to a summer peak, then fall in autumn and winter.
gemini.overview: The region is known for its karst mountains, steep limestone peaks that rise abruptly from flat plains and river valleys. The signature view is the Li River, where boats pass between the peaks, while the Yulong River offers a quieter version on bamboo rafts. The scenery is best seen from spring through autumn, when the rivers run high and the vegetation is green.

blurbs.text: Winter brings low water levels on the rivers, which can affect boat trips. The karst peaks are often shrouded in mist, giving them a moody appearance, but the vegetation is less vibrant and the skies are frequently overcast.
Spring rains raise the river levels, improving the boat and raft trips. The karst peaks are shrouded in mist, with the first fresh green of the year.

Spring rains keep the river levels up for the boat and raft trips. The karst peaks are bright green with new growth, and the frequent mist creates the classic, atmospheric views seen in traditional paintings.

The rivers run high, making this the best time for the Li River cruises and Yulong River rafts. The karst peaks are lush and green, and clear days give sharp reflections in the water, though summer haze can occasionally soften the views.
The weather is drier and the skies are often clear, provideing sharp views of the karst mountains. River levels are dropping, but the boat trips still run, and the autumn light highlights the peaks.

gemini.depth_why: Scores drop slightly during the wet season and hurricane risk months.
gemini.overview: The island pairs coastal views with striking karst formations, most notably the steep limestone mogotes rising from the tobacco fields of the Viñales Valley. The colonial architecture of Old Havana and the sea wall of the Malecón provide a classic urban backdrop against the water. The dry season from late autumn to spring offers the clearest skies for driving and photography.

blurbs.text: Dry, clear weather keeps the roads to the Viñales Valley open and provides sharp visibility for coastal drives along the Malecón.
Summer brings heavier rain showers that can briefly obscure valley views and soften the dirt roads in rural areas, though the limestone hills remain green.
The peak of the wet season carries a risk of tropical storms, which can wash out rural routes and limit access to coastal viewpoints.

gemini.depth_why: The scenery changes distinctly with the heavy winter snows, the spring melt, the lush summer hills, and the autumn foliage.
gemini.overview: Hokkaido is known for its vast, open natural spaces, featuring volcanic mountains, caldera lakes, and rolling rural hills. Lake Mashu holds deep, clear water, and the patchwork fields of Biei bloom with lavender and other flowers in July. Coastal views include the rugged Shiretoko Peninsula, where drift ice arrives from the north during the coldest months.

blurbs.text: Heavy snow covers the volcanic peaks and rural hills. Drift ice from the Sea of Okhotsk reaches the Shiretoko Peninsula, creating a frozen coastal expanse.
The deep winter snowpack is melting, leaving the mountains and fields muddy and brown. High-elevation passes and trails often remain blocked by snow.
Spring arrives late, bringing fresh green to the lower valleys and plains. The caldera lakes, including Lake Mashu, can be visited as the last of the lowland snow disappears.
The rolling hills of Biei are patchworks of early summer crops and flowers, and the air is clear over the volcanic ranges in Daisetsuzan National Park.
Lavender fields around Furano and Biei bloom in purple rows beside bands of other flowers, with clear views of the volcanic ranges in Daisetsuzan National Park.
Sunflowers and other late flowers color the fields around Furano and Biei, and the weather allows clear views of the volcanic ranges and the rugged northern coastlines.
Autumn colors sweep down from the high peaks of Daisetsuzan, turning the mountain forests red and gold. The crisp air provides sharp visibility across the caldera lakes.
The autumn foliage drops, leaving the forests bare before the heavy winter snows accumulate. Low clouds and early snowfalls obscure the higher mountain passes.

gemini.depth_why: Visibility and access to viewpoints change with the summer monsoon and humidity.
gemini.overview: Hong Kong has a dramatic urban setting, where steep, forested mountains drop directly into the sea. The signature view is the dense, illuminated skyline seen from Victoria Peak, best viewed on clear evenings. Beyond the city, the territory includes rugged coastlines, outlying islands, and hiking trails like the Dragon's Back that offer sweeping views of the South China Sea.

blurbs.text: Cooler, drier air brings the clearest skies of the year. Visibility from Victoria Peak and the coastal hiking trails is at its best, with sharp views across the harbor and out to the islands.
Spring brings rising humidity and frequent fog. Low clouds can obscure the tops of the mountains and the skyline from higher viewpoints, though coastal walks are still possible.
The summer monsoon brings heavy showers and high humidity, with occasional typhoons. Haze and downpours often reduce visibility, though green hillsides rise from the harbor on clearer days.
The heavy rains are lighter and humidity drops. Clearer days improve the views from the peaks and make the coastal trails more reliable.

gemini.depth_why: Scores rise through spring to a summer plateau, peak in October for fall foliage, and drop in winter.
gemini.overview: The Hudson Valley is known for its rolling, forested hills and the wide river that cuts through them. The Catskill Mountains provide a backdrop of modest peaks and deep cloves, while the river itself is lined with historic estates and viewpoints. The scenery peaks in autumn when the hardwood forests turn bright red and gold.

blurbs.text: The deciduous forests are bare, leaving the hillsides gray and brown. Snow often covers the higher elevations in the Catskills, though the main river valley sees less accumulation. Views are stark and open.
The forests are mostly bare with a first pale green haze at the branch tips. Waterfalls in the Catskills and along the river run high with snowmelt and spring rain.
The forests fill with fresh green leaves, and waterfalls in the Catskills and along the river still run well from spring rain.
The hills and valleys are thick with deep green foliage. The river views are framed by dense canopies, and the higher elevations offer a break from the summer heat.
The first color shows in the higher Catskills by late September, with the hardwood forests turning from green to red, orange and yellow at the highest elevations.
The hardwood forests put on a bright display of red, orange and yellow, with peak color moving down into the river valley by mid-to-late October.
The leaves have fallen and the landscape takes on a muted palette of browns and grays.
The landscape stays muted in browns and grays, and early snows can dust the Catskill peaks.

gemini.depth_why: Scores rise through spring to a summer peak, then fall through autumn as daylight and weather change.
gemini.overview: Ireland is known for its dramatic Atlantic coastline and green, rolling countryside. The Cliffs of Moher drop sheer into the ocean, while the Ring of Kerry and the Dingle Peninsula offer winding coastal drives past rugged headlands. Inland, the lakes and bogs of Connemara provide a quieter, moody landscape of low mountains and water.

blurbs.text: Short days and frequent winter storms limit time for coastal drives and walks. The scenery is often hidden by low clouds and rain, though the dramatic seas at the Cliffs of Moher can be striking when visible.
Longer daylight makes it easier to drive the Ring of Kerry or explore Connemara. Weather is unpredictable, but the countryside is greening and visibility improves between passing showers.
Long summer days provide the most time to explore the coasts and peninsulas. The weather is at its most stable for clear views of the cliffs and the Atlantic, though low clouds can still roll in.
Autumn colors show in the inland bogs and hillsides, and the days are still long enough for the main coastal viewpoints.
Autumn colors show in the inland bogs and hillsides. Daylight shortens noticeably by late in the month and coastal winds pick up, but the main viewpoints can still be visited.

gemini.depth_why: The skyline stays the same, but winter rain and low cloud dull it.
gemini.overview: Istanbul is known for its setting on the Bosphorus Strait, where the city's skyline of domes and minarets rises above the water. The views of the Golden Horn and the coastlines dividing Europe and Asia provide a striking maritime backdrop to the urban landscape.

blurbs.text: Rain and low cloud often dull the skyline, but clear spells give crisp views of the mosques and the Bosphorus from the ferries and waterfront promenades.
Long, mostly clear days show the silhouette of the mosques against the sky from the ferries and the waterfront promenades.

gemini.depth_why: The scenery is accessible and largely unchanged throughout the year.
gemini.overview: Jamaica is known for its dramatic coasts and lush interior. The island features steep cliffs along the western shore at Negril, while the eastern end rises into the forested peaks of the Blue Mountains. Inland, rivers cut through the tropical vegetation, creating cascades like Dunn's River Falls.

blurbs.text: The coastal cliffs, mountain roads, and waterfalls are visible and accessible. The tropical forests remain green, and the rivers flow steadily, allowing visitors to see the island's varied terrain.

gemini.depth_why: Scores dip slightly in winter and mid-summer due to weather extremes affecting the outdoor experience, but remain very high year-round.
gemini.overview: The region holds some of the world's most striking desert and canyon scenery, anchored by the red sandstone formations of Wadi Rum and the carved facades of Petra. Visitors walk through the narrow, towering walls of the Siq to reach the Treasury, while Wadi Rum offers vast expanses of dunes and sheer rock mountains. The landscapes are best seen in spring and autumn, when the light and temperatures are most favorable for exploring.

blurbs.text: Winter brings cooler temperatures and occasional rain or even light snow, which can briefly alter the look of the red rocks. The canyons and desert expanses are open to visitors, though the days are shorter for long hikes.
Spring gives clear skies and comfortable temperatures for walking the Siq or taking a jeep tour through Wadi Rum. The light on the sandstone is excellent, and the desert is at its most welcoming.

Summer heat is intense, especially in the open desert of Wadi Rum and the exposed areas of Petra. Early mornings and late afternoons are the only practical times to view the scenery, though the landscapes themselves are unchanged.
Autumn brings ideal conditions for exploring the canyons and dunes. The lowering sun casts deep shadows across the rock faces, highlighting the carved details in Petra and the vast scale of Wadi Rum.

gemini.depth_why: Scores drop in the summer as extreme heat limits physical access to the exposed desert trails.
gemini.overview: The region is known for its stark desert environments, featuring massive boulder piles and the distinct, spiky silhouettes of Joshua trees. Visitors drive through arid valleys or hike into palm-shaded canyons tucked into the San Jacinto Mountains. The best views require walking into the exposed landscape, making the cooler months the safest and most practical time to explore.

blurbs.text: Cool temperatures allow for long hikes into the exposed boulder fields and palm oases. The low winter sun casts long shadows across the desert floor, highlighting the rugged texture of the San Jacinto Mountains.
Rising heat begins to limit midday exploration. Early mornings offer clear views of the arid valleys before the sun makes the unshaded trails uncomfortable.
High temperatures make long hikes dangerous. Visitors mostly stick to scenic drives through the park, stepping out briefly at roadside pullouts to see the rock formations.
Extreme summer heat restricts access to the landscape. The desert is best viewed from the safety of an air-conditioned car or during very short walks just after dawn.
The desert remains intensely hot, keeping most trails empty. Sunset drives give the safest way to see the Joshua trees silhouetted against the sky.
Cooling weather reopens the longer trails. Hikers can safely return to the canyons and boulder piles as the midday heat becomes manageable again.

gemini.depth_why: Scores drop significantly during the summer monsoon when heavy rain floods the river valleys and obscures the hills, creating distinct seasonal stages.
gemini.overview: The vast Brahmaputra River and its surrounding floodplains define the scenery of Assam and Northeast India. Sunrise over the water and the tall riverine grasslands provides the region's signature view. Beyond the river valleys, the landscape shifts to dense forests and rolling hills that offer quiet, remote vistas. In the hills of Meghalaya, waterfalls drop from the plateau edge and living root bridges cross forest streams.

blurbs.text: Dry, clear weather keeps the roads open and the views sharp. The Brahmaputra is calm, and morning mist over the grasslands creates distinct sunrise views.
Pre-monsoon showers green the valleys and forests. Cloud cover is higher, and rising river levels alter the floodplain landscapes.

Heavy monsoon rains flood the Brahmaputra and its surrounding grasslands. Low clouds obscure the hills, and washed-out roads block access to many remote viewpoints. The waterfalls of the Meghalaya hills run at their fullest.
The heaviest rains taper off, leaving the forests and valleys deeply green. Water levels remain high, and lingering clouds often hide the hills.
The skies clear after the monsoon, revealing sharp views of the lush, rain-washed forests. The river begins to recede, exposing the floodplains again.

gemini.depth_why: Scores dip during the heavy rains of April and May, and slightly during the short rains of November.
gemini.overview: The defining view here is the flat, open savanna stretching toward the horizon, punctuated by acacia trees. In Amboseli, the backdrop is the massive, snow-capped cone of Mount Kilimanjaro rising directly from the plains. The landscapes are best seen when the skies are clear and the plains are dry.

blurbs.text: The plains are mostly dry and the skies are clear, offering sharp views of Mount Kilimanjaro from Amboseli and sweeping vistas across the Mara.
Heavy rains turn the plains green and fill the seasonal waterholes. The skies are often cloudy, which can obscure the view of Kilimanjaro, and some dirt tracks become difficult to navigate.
The long dry season brings clear skies and dusty, golden plains. The views across the savanna are unobstructed, and Mount Kilimanjaro is often visible in the early mornings and late afternoons.
Short rains bring brief afternoon showers and green up the savanna. The skies can be dramatic with storm clouds, though the mountains may be hidden at times.

gemini.depth_why: Scores drop during the heavy monsoon rains when visibility and access are reduced, then recover.
gemini.overview: Kerala is known for its waterways and lush greenery, anchored by the famous backwaters where houseboats drift past palm-lined canals and lakes. Inland, the Western Ghats rise into rolling hills covered in dense forests and the manicured tea estates of Munnar. The coast offers long stretches of sandy beaches along the Arabian Sea.

blurbs.text: Clear skies and dry weather make this the best time to see the landscapes. The backwaters are calm for cruising, and the tea hills of Munnar are bright and visible without the heavy cloud cover of the wet season.
Heat and humidity build, bringing occasional pre-monsoon showers. Haze can sometimes soften the views over the Western Ghats, but the backwaters and hill stations are still worth visiting.

The southwest monsoon brings heavy, persistent rain. While the forests and tea estates turn a vibrant, lush green, low clouds often obscure the hills, and heavy downpours can disrupt houseboat travel on the backwaters.

The heaviest rains pass, leaving the landscapes washed and intensely green. Waterfalls are at their fullest, though a lighter northeast monsoon can still bring afternoon showers that briefly hide the hills.

gemini.depth_why: Scores rise through the dry season to peak in July and August, then fall as the wet season approaches.
gemini.overview: Komodo and Flores are known for their dramatic coastal scenery, where rugged, dry islands rise sharply from clear waters. The signature view is from the viewpoint on Padar Island, looking down over curved bays with different colored sands, including the famous pink beaches. The landscapes are best seen by boat during the dry season, when the skies are clear and the seas are calm. On Flores, the three crater lakes of Kelimutu change color over time.

blurbs.text: The wet season brings heavy rain and rough seas, making boat travel between the islands difficult or impossible. The usually dry, brown hills turn green, but heavy cloud cover often obscures the views.
The rains ease and the seas are calmer, giving access to the islands. The hillsides are green from the wet season, offering a different look to the rugged coastlines.

Clear skies and calm waters make for the best views of the islands. The vegetation is dry, giving the hills their characteristic rugged, brown appearance that contrasts sharply with the blue water and pink sands.
Humidity is building toward the wet season and clouds gather more often, though skies are mostly clear and the coastal views are strong.
Clouds and humidity build as the wet season nears, and showers can soften the light on the islands.
The wet season is close, with more cloud and seas that can turn choppy, though the coastal views are still reachable on clear mornings.

gemini.depth_why: The bush is green after the summer rains and dry and golden-brown through the winter.
gemini.overview: Kruger and Sabi Sands are known for vast stretches of open bushveld, dry riverbeds, and scattered waterholes. The scenery is subtle, with flat plains and low woodlands that are green from November to April and golden-brown from May to October. The views are best appreciated during the golden hours of early morning and late afternoon, when the light softens the harsh plains. The Blyde River Canyon and the Panorama Route, on the escarpment west of the park, add cliffs that drop more than 2,000 feet.

blurbs.text: The rains leave the bushveld green and full of wildflowers, with storm clouds over the plains and the rivers running full. Mist and storm cloud often hide the viewpoints at Blyde River Canyon.
The grass is golden and the trees still hold green leaves, with clear skies and soft light across the plains.

The bushveld is dry and golden-brown, the trees are bare and the riverbeds are mostly dry. The best views come at sunrise and sunset, when low light warms the grass. Clear air gives long views from the Blyde River Canyon viewpoints.
The plains are still dry and brown, but the first showers can bring a haze of fresh green and dramatic storm clouds to the horizon.
Early rains turn the bush green and fill the waterholes, and storm clouds give the skies drama.

gemini.depth_why: Scores rise from winter closures to a summer peak when high passes and lakes are accessible.
gemini.overview: Kyrgyzstan is known for the Tian Shan mountains, a vast range of high peaks, deep valleys and alpine lakes. The scenery is rugged and remote, with sweeping views of the high-altitude Song-Köl and the massive Issyk-Kul. Summer opens the high passes and valleys, while winter snow closes much of the backcountry.

blurbs.text: Deep snow shuts the high passes and remote valleys, cutting off access to Song-Köl and much of the backcountry. The lower valleys and the shores of Issyk-Kul remain visible, but travel is limited.
Snow still blocks the highest routes and alpine lakes. The scenery is stark, and access to the deep mountains is difficult.
Snow melts from the lower valleys, though the highest routes and alpine lakes are still blocked. The scenery is stark, and access to the deep mountains remains difficult.
The lower and mid-elevation valleys are clear, offering views of the surrounding peaks. The highest passes and lakes like Song-Köl may still be blocked by late snow.
The high passes are open, giving access to the remote alpine scenery of the Tian Shan. The sweeping views around Song-Köl and the vast expanse of Issyk-Kul are within reach.
The lower and mid-elevation valleys are clear, giving views of the surrounding peaks. Early autumn storms can block the highest passes and lakes like Song-Köl.
The first snows of winter dust the lower valleys, and the highest routes and alpine lakes are blocked. The scenery is stark, and access to the deep mountains is difficult.

gemini.depth_why: The high mountain passes dictate access to the scenery, creating distinct stages of winter closure, spring melting, and full summer access.
gemini.overview: High-altitude desert mountains define the region, with stark, barren ridges dropping into deep river valleys. The signature views include the high-altitude blue waters of Pangong Lake, the sand dunes of the Nubra Valley, and Buddhist monasteries perched on steep cliffs. The high mountain passes that connect these areas are only clear of snow during the short summer.

blurbs.text: Heavy winter snow blocks the high passes, cutting off road access to the lakes and valleys outside Leh. The landscape is frozen and white.
Snow melts in the lower valleys, but the major mountain passes remain blocked by deep drifts, keeping the wider region inaccessible by road.
Plows clear the main highways and lower passes, opening the first overland routes into the region. The high lakes remain partially frozen.
The high passes, including Khardung La, are open, allowing drives to the Nubra Valley dunes and the bright blue expanse of Pangong Lake. The skies are clear and the barren mountains are in full view.
Autumn turns the valley willows and poplars yellow against the stark mountains. Early snows can temporarily close the high passes.
Deep cold sets in and snow accumulates on the roads. The high passes close for the season, restricting travel to the immediate surroundings of Leh.

gemini.depth_why: Scores rise through spring to a summer peak, then fall through autumn as weather and daylight reduce access to the fells.
gemini.overview: The Lake District is known for its deep glacial ribbon lakes set among England's highest mountains, known locally as fells. Windermere and Derwentwater provide the classic valley views, while the high ridges of Helvellyn and Scafell Pike offer sweeping panoramas over the rugged terrain.

blurbs.text: Short days and frequent low cloud or rain often obscure the high fells. Snow can cover the peaks, making the ridges challenging to reach, though the lower valleys and lakeshores still give views.
Lengthening daylight brings clearer views. The high fells may still hold patches of snow, while the valleys green up.
Long daylight hours allow for extensive walks on the high ridges like Helvellyn. The lakes and valleys are fully green, and visibility is generally at its best for taking in the sweeping panoramas.
Autumn color peaks in the wooded valleys and lower slopes, contrasting with the bare rock of the fells. Daylight shortens noticeably, and low cloud becomes more common on the heights.

gemini.depth_why: The scenery changes distinctly with the snowpack, the autumn foliage, and the extreme shifts in daylight.
gemini.overview: Finnish Lapland is known for its vast forests of pine and birch and its countless lakes. Rounded, treeless fells rise above the timberline, providing long views over the remote terrain. The scenery shifts heavily with the seasons, from deep winter snowscapes to bright autumn foliage.

blurbs.text: The polar night limits daylight to a few hours of blue twilight, leaving the forests and fells mostly hidden in darkness.
Deep snow blankets the pine trees and freezes the lakes solid. Rapidly lengthening days provide clear, bright views of the winter landscape from the fell tops.
Melting snow leaves the ground muddy and the lakes in a state of thaw, dulling the landscape before the summer green arrives.
The midnight sun keeps the dense forests and flowing rivers visible around the clock. Trails over the treeless fells are clear of snow.
Autumn colors turn the birch forests and low ground cover across the fells bright yellow and red.
The leaves drop and daylight fades rapidly. The terrain often looks gray and slushy before the permanent winter snowpack settles.

gemini.depth_why: The hills and river stay the same, but winter rain and gray skies dull the views.
gemini.overview: Lisbon is known for its steep hills, tiled facades, and the wide Tagus River. Viewpoints known as miradouros look out over terracotta roofs to the water, while the nearby coast offers sandy beaches and rocky cliffs.

blurbs.text: Rain and gray skies come and go, but the hills still give clear vantage points over the Tagus River on bright days.
Mild, bright days make the viewpoints over the historic neighborhoods and the Tagus River pleasant.
Clear skies and strong light show the terracotta roofs and the Tagus River from the city's hills, and the coast toward Cascais is bright and open.
Soft autumn light warms the hillside neighborhoods and the river, though the first rains can dull the views.

gemini.depth_why: The scenery changes with the dramatic shifts in daylight and snow cover across the seasons.
gemini.overview: The Lofoten Islands are known for steep coastal mountains that rise directly from the sea, sheltering traditional fishing villages. The signature views center on the red cabins of Reine and Hamnøy set against jagged peaks, while the steep hike up Reinebringen provides a high vantage point over the fjords. The best visibility and trail access happens during the summer months.

blurbs.text: The sun barely rises, leaving only a few hours of blue twilight to see the snow-covered peaks and fjords.
Daylight is back and growing quickly, lighting the dramatic winter landscapes, though high trails are buried in snow.
Snow melts from the lower elevations and days grow long, opening up coastal walks and lower viewpoints.
The midnight sun provides continuous daylight for viewing the fjords, and steep trails like Reinebringen are clear of snow.
Autumn brings golden colors to the coastal grasses, though increasing rain and low clouds often obscure the mountain peaks.
Daylight fades rapidly and early snow begins to cover the mountains, limiting visibility and access to high viewpoints.

gemini.depth_why: The skyline stays the same, but the parks and riverbanks are greener and brighter in the warm half of the year.
gemini.overview: London's scenery is its urban riverfront. The Thames cuts through the center, offering sweeping views of the skyline from the water, bridges, and high vantage points. The signature panorama stretches from Tower Bridge to the modern towers of the city.

blurbs.text: Bare trees and gray skies leave the parks brown and muted, but the Thames skyline still looks sharp from the high walkways of Tower Bridge and the observation decks of the Shard.
Blossom and fresh green fill the parks and riverbanks, softening the Thames skyline.
Green parks and long daylight frame the Thames skyline, best seen from the high walkways of Tower Bridge or the observation decks of the Shard.
Autumn colors turn the parks gold and red along the river, though skies are often overcast.

gemini.depth_why: The desert and coastal landscapes remain static and accessible across the seasons.
gemini.overview: The region is known for the sharp contrast between arid desert terrain and the waters of the Pacific Ocean and Sea of Cortez. The signature view is El Arco at Land's End, a massive natural stone arch rising from the sea at the tip of the Baja California peninsula. Inland, the landscape transitions into dry, cactus-studded canyons and rugged hills.

blurbs.text: The coastal rocks and desert canyons remain fully visible and accessible. Boats run out to Land's End to view El Arco and the surrounding granite pinnacles from the water. Inland dirt roads lead through dry washes and scrub-covered hills.

gemini.depth_why: Scores change with the dry season, the smoky season, and the monsoon rains.
gemini.overview: Laos is known for the Mekong River winding through forested mountains. Boats drift past green banks and small villages, and the tiered turquoise pools of Kuang Si Falls sit deep in the northern forest. Farther out are quiet rice valleys and limestone caves.

blurbs.text: Clear skies and dry roads make it easy to reach the viewpoints and caves. The rivers run clear, and the waterfalls have strong flow. The limestone peaks around Vang Vieng and Nong Khiaw stand out sharply against clear skies.
Agricultural fires fill the air with thick smoke, severely reducing visibility across the valleys. Water levels drop, leaving the falls and rivers much lower.
Heavy monsoon rains turn the rivers brown and swell them with runoff. Unpaved roads into the mountains often become muddy and difficult to pass, though the forests turn a vibrant green.
The rains taper off, leaving the karst mountains lush and the air clear of smoke. The rivers and waterfalls are full from the wet season, though some rural roads remain rutted.

gemini.depth_why: The wet and dry seasons dictate road access to the main geological sites, creating clear stages of accessibility.
gemini.overview: Madagascar is known for its dense rainforests, coastal stretches, and striking geological formations. The signature views include the towering baobab trees lining dirt roads in the west and the sharp limestone pinnacles of the Tsingy de Bemaraha. Access to these remote landscapes depends heavily on the dry season, as unpaved routes become impassable in the rain.

blurbs.text: Heavy rains and cyclones wash out dirt roads across the country. Remote reserves and the limestone forests are inaccessible, leaving only a few paved coastal and highland routes open.
The rains are easing, but deep mud still blocks access to many western and northern landscapes, and the sharp limestone pinnacles are closed.
Rains are lighter and some forest reserves can be reached again, though the sharp limestone pinnacles usually remain closed and mud lingers on the western tracks.
The dry season takes hold, drying out the unpaved routes. The Tsingy de Bemaraha typically opens to visitors, and the Avenue of the Baobabs is easily reached under clear skies.
Clear, dry weather provides the best conditions for driving the rough roads to the western baobabs and northern coasts. The limestone canyons and dense eastern rainforests can be reached.
The first rains of the wet season are back, turning dust to mud again. The main viewpoints are still reachable early on, but deep forest routes and canyon trails are harder to navigate.
The wet season sets in, bringing heavy downpours that flood river crossings. The Tsingy de Bemaraha closes for the season, and overland travel to the baobabs becomes unreliable.

gemini.depth_why: Scores form clear seasonal groups based on rainfall and cloud cover affecting visibility and trail access.
gemini.overview: Madeira's volcanic landscape rises steeply from the Atlantic, defined by sharp mountain ridges, deep ravines, and ancient laurel forests. The island is known for its levadas, a network of historic irrigation channels that double as walking trails past waterfalls and sheer drops. High coastal cliffs like Cabo Girão and the jagged peaks around Pico do Arieiro are the most famous viewpoints.

blurbs.text: Rain and low clouds frequently obscure the high peaks and coastal viewpoints. Wet conditions can make the narrow levada trails muddy and prone to minor rockfalls, though the lower coastal paths are easier going.

Cloud lifts from the central mountains more often, showing the deep valleys. The levada trails dry out, making the walks through the laurel forests and past the island's waterfalls much easier to navigate.

Clear skies provide the most reliable visibility for the jagged ridges connecting Pico do Arieiro and Pico Ruivo. The high coastal cliffs at Cabo Girão stand out sharply against the ocean, and the forest trails are largely dry.
Autumn brings returning moisture, with fog often settling into the laurel forests and upper ravines. The main mountain viewpoints are visible on clearer days, but the trails soften with early rains.

gemini.depth_why: The year divides into a clear dry season with optimal visibility and a cloudier wet season.
gemini.overview: The defining view of the Maldives is its vast network of coral atolls, best seen from above on a seaplane flight. Thousands of low-lying islands form rings of white sand and palm trees surrounded by shallow, bright turquoise lagoons that drop off into the deep blue Indian Ocean. At water level, the scenery consists of endless horizons and isolated sandbanks.

blurbs.text: Clear skies and calm weather maximize visibility for flights over the atolls and keep the contrast between the shallow reefs and the deep ocean sharp.
The southwest monsoon brings heavier clouds and frequent rain showers, which can temporarily obscure aerial views and dull the bright colors of the lagoons.

gemini.depth_why: The mountains and cliffs stay the same, but winter cloud and midsummer haze soften the views.
gemini.overview: Mallorca is known for the steep limestone peaks of the Serra de Tramuntana dropping directly into the Mediterranean Sea. The island's dramatic coastal views are the primary scenic draw, particularly along the rugged northern and western shores where winding roads connect mountain passes to hidden coves. Villages like Sóller and Deià sit nestled in terraced valleys, with historic stone architecture contrasting with the green hillsides.

blurbs.text: Rain and low cloud sometimes hide the Serra de Tramuntana, but clear days give sharp views of the cliffs and the terraced valleys around Sóller and Deià.
Green hillsides and wildflowers cover the Tramuntana, and mild, clear days show the cliffs of the Formentor peninsula and the stone villages of Sóller and Deià.
Strong sun and heat haze soften the distant views, so the Formentor cliffs and the terraced valleys are best at sunrise and sunset.
Warm, clear days and a calm sea show the Tramuntana cliffs, the olive groves and the stone villages of Sóller and Deià.

gemini.depth_why: Scores follow the seasons, with summer offering the best conditions for coastal access and winter bringing shorter, cooler days.
gemini.overview: The region is known for its intricate coastlines, from the golden beaches of Abel Tasman National Park to the sunken river valleys of the Marlborough Sounds. Visitors explore the forested shores and clear waters by kayak, water taxi, or on foot along coastal tracks. The scenery is best viewed from the water or the trails that trace the peninsulas and bays.

blurbs.text: Long, warm days highlight the golden sands and clear waters of the coast. Kayaks and water taxis run frequently, making it easy to explore the bays and forested headlands of Abel Tasman and the Marlborough Sounds.
Cooler air brings quieter trails. The coastal forests remain green, and the waters of the sounds are often calm and reflective, though shorter days mean less time for long hikes or paddles.
Crisp, short days and cooler temperatures on the water. The scenery is striking and uncrowded, but boat schedules are reduced and the sea breeze can be chilly.
The coast is warming and the days are lengthening. The trails and waterways are busier as the weather improves for kayaking and hiking along the sounds and beaches.

gemini.depth_why: The scenery and access remain consistent throughout the year.
gemini.overview: Maui is known for its dramatic coasts, volcanic peaks, and lush waterfalls. The island's signature views include the sunrise over the Haleakalā crater and the dense rainforests along the Road to Hana.

blurbs.text: The drive to Hana reveals countless waterfalls and dense tropical foliage, while the summit of Haleakalā offers sweeping views of the crater and the surrounding ocean. The partially submerged volcanic crater of Molokini is visible off the coast.

gemini.depth_why: Scores form clear groups based on the wet and dry seasons affecting visibility and trail conditions.
gemini.overview: The island's defining views are its dramatic coastlines, anchored by the basalt monolith of Le Morne Brabant rising over a turquoise lagoon. The interior holds forested volcanic peaks, waterfalls, and the exposed multi-colored volcanic ash dunes at Chamarel. The clearest views and driest trails run from May through September.

blurbs.text: Heavy rains and occasional cyclones can obscure coastal views and leave inland trails to the waterfalls muddy.
Drier air and clear skies provide sharp visibility across the lagoons and the forested slopes of the Black River Gorges.
Humidity and cloud cover build, softening the light over the colored earths at Chamarel, though most coastal viewpoints are clear.

gemini.depth_why: Access to high mountain passes and the colors of the vineyards change with the seasons.
gemini.overview: The Andes mountains rise directly behind the region's vineyards, dominated by Aconcagua, the highest peak in the Americas. Drives toward the Chilean border pass through deep rocky canyons and the arid Uspallata valley.

blurbs.text: Clear weather gives access to the high-altitude trails of Aconcagua Provincial Park and the mountain passes. The valleys are bright green against the dry, rocky Andes.
The vineyards turn yellow and red, creating a sharp color contrast with the fresh snow capping the higher peaks.
Leaves drop from the vines and temperatures cool, though the lower mountain roads remain clear for drives toward the Chilean border.
Heavy snow blankets the high Andes, often closing the international pass and higher viewpoints. The lower valleys are bare, but the snow-capped backdrop is prominent.
Snowmelt fills the rivers, and the valleys are greening again. The high passes are reopening one by one as the snowline retreats.

gemini.depth_why: The plazas and canals stay the same, but clear air, smog and the rains change how much of the volcanoes shows.
gemini.overview: Mexico City sits in a high-altitude basin surrounded by distant volcanic peaks. The primary scenic draws are urban, centered on the vast Zócalo square and the ancient, tree-lined canals of Xochimilco in the south. Northeast of the city, the pyramids of Teotihuacan rise from a dry plain and are often seen at sunrise from a hot air balloon. On clear days, the snow-capped volcanoes Popocatépetl and Iztaccíhuatl can be seen on the horizon.

blurbs.text: Dry, clear air gives the best chance of seeing the snow-capped volcanoes Popocatépetl and Iztaccíhuatl above the Zócalo and the canals of Xochimilco.
Jacaranda trees bloom purple along the streets, though smog and haze often hide the volcanoes on the horizon.
Afternoon rain and cloud often hide the volcanoes, but the hills and parks are green and the canals of Xochimilco are full.

gemini.depth_why: Scores follow the seasons, peaking in the warmer summer months when trails are fully open and daylight is longest, and dipping in winter when snow and shorter days limit access.
gemini.overview: Milford Sound and Fiordland National Park are known for deep, glacier-carved fjords, sheer cliffs, and dense temperate rainforests. The signature view is Milford Sound itself, best seen from the water, where waterfalls cascade hundreds of feet down rock faces into the sea. The region is also known for the Milford Track, a multi-day hike through alpine passes and valleys, and is best visited in the warmer months when trails are clear of snow.

blurbs.text: Long daylight hours and warmer temperatures make this the best time to hike the Milford Track and explore the fjords by boat. The rainforests are lush, and the waterfalls flow heavily, especially after frequent rain.
Cooler temperatures and shorter days mark the month, but the main viewpoints and boat tours run normally. Snow may dust the higher peaks, adding contrast to the sheer cliffs.

Snow covers the mountains, shutting the Milford Track to independent hikers and limiting access to higher elevations. Boat tours on Milford Sound still run, offering clear, crisp days and views of snow-capped peaks, though daylight is short.
Snow lingers on the higher peaks, adding contrast to the sheer cliffs, and the main viewpoints and boat tours run normally. The Milford Track season starts near the end of the month.

gemini.depth_why: Scores rise from closed winter months to a summer peak, then fall in autumn.
gemini.overview: Mongolia is known for its vast, open spaces, from the rolling green steppe dotted with white gers to the towering sand dunes of the Gobi Desert. The landscape is largely untouched, offering immense skies and a sense of deep isolation. Lake Khuvsgul in the north provides a striking contrast with its deep blue waters surrounded by taiga forest.

blurbs.text: Extreme cold and heavy snow make travel across the steppe and desert nearly impossible. Most tourist camps are closed, and roads are impassable.
The snow begins to melt, but the landscape is often brown and muddy. High winds and dust storms frequently obscure views in the Gobi.
The steppe starts to turn green, and temperatures become mild enough for travel. Dust storms can still occur in the desert regions.
The steppe is lush and green, and the Gobi dunes are accessible. Lake Khuvsgul is clear of ice, reflecting the surrounding mountains and forests.
The landscape takes on golden autumn hues, particularly in the northern forests around Lake Khuvsgul. The air is crisp and clear, though nights are cold.
Snow begins to fall, and the cold returns quickly. Many camps close for the season, and travel becomes difficult as the month progresses.

gemini.depth_why: Scores dip slightly in winter due to rain and potential road closures, while the rest of the year is peak.
gemini.overview: The dramatic meeting of the Santa Lucia Mountains and the Pacific Ocean creates one of the world's premier coastal drives. Highway 1 winds along sheer cliffs above crashing surf, anchored by the iconic span of Bixby Creek Bridge. Point Lobos adds rocky coves near Monterey, and inland, dense groves of coastal redwoods fill the canyons.

blurbs.text: Winter storms bring heavy rain that can cause landslides and temporary closures along Highway 1. When the skies clear, the air is crisp and the coastal views are sharp, though the ocean is often rough.
Clear days and green hillsides line the coast. McWay Falls drops onto the beach, and the creeks in the redwood canyons run strong from winter rains.

The coastal highway and redwood trails are at their most reliable from summer through early fall. Morning fog often blankets the coastline, especially in early summer, usually burning off by afternoon to reveal the cliffs and ocean.

gemini.depth_why: Clear skies and snow contrast define the long peak season, while summer heat haze obscures the views.
gemini.overview: The region contrasts the dense urban maze of Marrakech's medina with the towering peaks of the High Atlas mountains. Deep valleys and high mountain passes provide sweeping views of snow-capped ridges and traditional stone villages. The landscape transitions eastward into arid gorges and sand dunes of the vast Sahara desert.

blurbs.text: Clear air provides sharp views of the High Atlas peaks from the plains, with winter snow adding bright contrast to the mountains.
Rising temperatures bring a heat haze that begins to obscure the distant mountain ridges from the city.
Intense summer heat creates a thick haze over the plains, hiding the mountains and making the desert dunes difficult to reach and view.
The intense heat haze lifts, slowly revealing the mountain backdrop and opening up the desert routes.

gemini.depth_why: Scores peak in the dry winter months when skies are clear and access is easiest, dipping slightly in the hotter, wetter summer.
gemini.overview: Namibia is known for its vast, ancient deserts and stark coastal landscapes. The towering red dunes of Sossusvlei rise above the white clay pan of Deadvlei and its skeletal preserved trees. The Skeleton Coast offers a desolate, shipwreck-dotted shoreline where the desert meets the Atlantic Ocean. The dry months from May to October provide the clearest skies and easiest access to remote areas.

blurbs.text: Intense heat and occasional rains can make some remote dirt roads challenging to navigate. The dunes at Sossusvlei remain striking, though the midday sun is fierce, making early morning the best time to view the deep red sands.

Dry weather brings clear, bright skies that highlight the stark contrasts of the desert landscapes. The cooler temperatures make exploring the dunes of Sossusvlei and the desolate stretches of the Skeleton Coast more comfortable, with excellent visibility for photography.

gemini.depth_why: Scores rise through spring as vines leaf out, peak in late summer and early fall with full canopies and harvest colors, and drop in winter when vines are bare.
gemini.overview: The draw here is the classic wine country landscape of rolling hills covered in neat rows of grapevines. The scenery is rural and cultivated, with oak-studded ridges framing the valley floors. The views change with the seasons, from bright green spring growth to golden autumn foliage, best seen from the winding valley roads or hillside viewpoints. To the west, the Sonoma Coast adds sea cliffs and coves, and coast redwoods grow along the Russian River.

blurbs.text: The vines are dormant and bare, leaving the valleys looking stark. Winter rains turn the surrounding hillsides bright green, and wild mustard often blooms between the vine rows, adding patches of yellow to the landscape.
Bud break brings bright green leaves to the vineyards, and the surrounding hills stay green from the winter rains.

The vineyard canopies are full and lush, creating a sea of green across the valley floors and lower hillsides. The surrounding uncultivated hills have turned their typical summer gold, contrasting with the irrigated vines. Fog often covers the Sonoma Coast in the mornings and evenings.
The vines are heavy with fruit under a full green canopy, and the surrounding hills are summer gold. Fog often covers the Sonoma Coast in the mornings and evenings.

The vines are heavy with fruit and the harvest is underway. The valleys take on autumn colors, with patches of yellow, gold, and deep red across the vineyards. Fog is less persistent on the Sonoma Coast.
The autumn color fades and the vines stand bare for the winter. The landscape is quiet, and the winter rains green the surrounding hillsides.

gemini.depth_why: Visibility and access change with the monsoon and winter snows.
gemini.overview: Nepal holds some of the highest mountain scenery on Earth, anchored by the Himalayas. Visitors come for the towering peaks of Everest and Annapurna, massive glaciers, and the terraced hillsides of the Kathmandu Valley. The clearest views of the high peaks come in autumn and spring.

blurbs.text: Winter brings crisp, clear skies for mountain viewing, though heavy snow can block high-altitude trekking passes. Lower elevation viewpoints still provide excellent sights of the snow-capped peaks.

Spring warms the valleys and forests, adding blooming rhododendrons to the lower slopes. The high peaks are clearest in the early morning, but pre-monsoon haze dulls the long views for much of the day.
Heavy monsoon clouds and rain obscure the mountains for days at a time. Trekking routes become muddy, and flights to high-altitude airstrips are frequently delayed by poor visibility.

Monsoon clouds and rain still hide the mountains for days at a time, though the breaks are longer and the lower hills are green. Trekking routes are muddy, and flights to high-altitude airstrips are often delayed by poor visibility.
The skies clear after the monsoon, revealing the sharpest views of Everest and the Annapurna range. Trails and flights offer unobstructed panoramas of the high Himalayas.
The air remains clear and dry, giving sharp views of the mountains before the heaviest winter snows arrive to block the highest passes.

gemini.depth_why: The streets and bayous stay the same, but spring is bright and green and summer heat and humidity keep people indoors.
gemini.overview: New Orleans scenery is defined by the historic urban core and surrounding wetlands. The primary sights are the wrought-iron balconies and narrow streets of the French Quarter, alongside the slow-moving waters of the nearby bayous. The environment is entirely flat, with ancient live oaks draped in Spanish moss providing the main natural backdrop.

blurbs.text: Dry, comfortable air and soft light make the French Quarter streets, the bayous and the moss-draped live oaks pleasant to see.
Cool, mild days make the French Quarter streets and the bayous easy to explore, though gray skies often mute the moss-draped live oaks.
Warm, green weather brings fresh leaves to the live oaks, and flowering trees and azaleas brighten the streets around the French Quarter.
Heat in the 90s Fahrenheit and heavy humidity keep most viewing to the early morning and evening, though the bayous and live oaks are at their greenest.

gemini.depth_why: Scores change with the transition between the clear dry season and the cloudy, muddy wet season.
gemini.overview: Nicaragua's landscape is defined by its chain of volcanoes, crater lakes, and colonial architecture set against natural backdrops. Visitors can drive through high-elevation cloud forests to reach the rims of active volcanic calderas. The Pacific coast holds rugged beaches.

blurbs.text: Clear skies give the best visibility for looking down into volcano craters or across the lakes. The landscape is still green from the recent rains, and dirt roads to remote viewpoints are dry and passable.
The dry weather keeps roads open, though dust and agricultural smoke can create a haze that obscures distant mountain views.
The rains turn the forests and hillsides a deep green. Clouds often build up in the afternoons, hiding the volcano peaks, but mornings usually stay clear enough for coastal and lake views.
Heavy rains wash out unpaved roads and trails to higher elevations. Thick cloud cover frequently blocks the views of the calderas and valleys.
The heavy rains taper off, leaving the cloud forests and volcanic slopes lush. Visibility improves as the skies begin to clear.

gemini.depth_why: The coast stays the same, but winter storms and summer haze affect how clear the views are.
gemini.overview: The French Riviera is known for its Mediterranean coastline, where steep hills drop into blue water. The scenery centers on the contrast between the sea and the perched hilltop villages that overlook it. The Promenade des Anglais in Nice and the high vantage point of Èze provide the most recognizable views of this coastal stretch.

blurbs.text: Mild, crisp days give sharp views of the sea and the snow-capped Alps behind the coast, though storms can bring gray skies and rough water.
Wildflowers and fresh green hills frame clear blue water, and the air is mild and clear for views from the hilltop villages and Èze.
Bright sun and deep blue water suit the beach promenades and hilltop viewpoints, though summer haze can soften the farthest views.
Warm water and soft light give good coastal views, though heavy autumn rain can bring gray skies and rough seas.

gemini.depth_why: Scores change significantly based on the seasonal closure of the main highway and snowpack levels.
gemini.overview: North Cascades National Park is known for its jagged peaks, deep forested valleys, and over 300 glaciers. The main draw is the North Cascades Highway, which winds past the turquoise waters of Diablo Lake and offers views of Mount Shuksan. The rugged terrain provides quiet, remote scenery for those willing to hike, with the best access from mid-summer to early fall.

blurbs.text: Heavy snow shuts the North Cascades Highway, cutting off access to the park's core and its famous viewpoints.
Heavy snow still blocks the North Cascades Highway while crews work to clear it, so the park's core and its famous viewpoints are out of reach.
The highway has usually reopened by now, and lower elevation forests can be reached, but high trails and passes remain buried in snow.
Melting snow feeds the rivers and waterfalls. The highway is open, though high-elevation trails may still have snow patches.
Glacial flour turns Diablo Lake a brilliant turquoise. High passes and trails are clear of snow, giving expansive views of the glaciers and Mount Shuksan.
Autumn brings yellow larches to the high passes, but early snowstorms begin to threaten access and visibility.
The North Cascades Highway is shut for the season, closing off the main scenic route through the mountains.

gemini.depth_why: Scores change gradually with the seasons, reflecting daylight and weather conditions for viewing the landscapes.
gemini.overview: The North Island is known for its volcanic core, where the geothermal landscapes around Rotorua and the volcanic peaks of Tongariro National Park are the major draws. Dense native forests cover much of the interior. The coast is a separate world, with subtropical bays and islands in the north and black-sand surf beaches along the west.

blurbs.text: Long days provide the best conditions for exploring the volcanic plateaus and coastal bays. The trails in Tongariro National Park are mostly clear of snow, and the geothermal areas around Rotorua are easy to visit.
Cooler temperatures and shorter days set in, but the volcanic landscapes and native forests are still very much in view. The coastal scenery is still clear, though the weather is more changeable.

Snow falls on the higher elevations of the central plateau, altering the look of the volcanic peaks. Coastal areas are cooler and wetter, and shorter daylight hours limit the time available for long scenic drives or hikes.

The snowline retreats on the central volcanoes and the native forests turn greener. The weather is often unsettled, but the lengthening days give more time to view the geothermal features and coastal bays.

gemini.depth_why: The scenery changes with the seasons, from snow and ice in winter to clear coastal views in summer and bright foliage in October.
gemini.overview: Nova Scotia is known for its rugged Atlantic coastline and dense forests. The Cabot Trail winds past steep ocean cliffs and highland woods, while the southern shores feature bare granite outcrops and the Peggy's Cove lighthouse. The views are clearest in summer, and the woods turn bright red and gold in October.

blurbs.text: Snow and ice cover the highlands, and winter storms bring heavy surf to the coast. Many secondary roads and trailheads are snowbound or difficult to drive.
Snow melts away and the forests green up. Coastal fog is common as the air warms over the cold Atlantic, sometimes hiding the ocean views.
Clear skies and warm air make driving the Cabot Trail and walking the coastal cliffs easy. The ocean views stretch far to the horizon, and the highland forests are deep green.
The broadleaf forests across the highlands and inland valleys turn bright red, orange, and yellow. The coastal drives are framed by the autumn colors.
The leaves have dropped and the woods are bare and gray. Coastal winds pick up, and early snow can dust the highlands.
The woods are bare and gray, and snow dusts the highlands as winter settles over the coast.

gemini.depth_why: The skyline stays the same, but Central Park is bare in winter, in blossom in spring and in color in fall, and summer is hot and hazy.
gemini.overview: The primary scenic draw here is the famous urban skyline, viewed across the harbor and rivers. Visitors take in the dense grid of skyscrapers from vantage points like the Brooklyn Bridge and the Empire State Building. Central Park's trees add blossoms in spring and gold and red leaves in fall.

blurbs.text: Bare trees and cold, often gray days leave Central Park brown, though snow can brighten the park and the skyline stays sharp from the Brooklyn Bridge and the Empire State Building.
Magnolias and cherry blossoms open in Central Park, and mild days make the Brooklyn Bridge and the Empire State Building comfortable vantage points for the skyline.
Fresh green leaves fill Central Park, and mild weather frames the skyline from the Brooklyn Bridge and the Empire State Building.
Hot, humid days with haze soften the skyline, though Central Park is fully green and the Brooklyn Bridge and the harbor are at their liveliest.
Warm, clear days give sharp skyline views from the Brooklyn Bridge and the Empire State Building.
Gold and red leaves fill Central Park, and crisp, clear air gives sharp skyline views from the Brooklyn Bridge and the Empire State Building.

gemini.depth_why: The scenery in Oaxaca is accessible year-round with no significant closures or changes in visibility that would alter the score.
gemini.overview: Oaxaca is known for its rugged mountains, deep valleys, and the striking petrified waterfalls of Hierve el Agua. The state's varied terrain includes high-altitude pine forests, arid valleys, and a rugged Pacific coastline. The ancient Zapotec city of Monte Albán offers sweeping views over the central valleys.

blurbs.text: The mountain roads and coastal highways are clear, giving access to the state's varied terrain. The mineral springs and petrified cascades at Hierve el Agua are visible against the valley backdrop, and the high-altitude ruins of Monte Albán provide clear views over the surrounding landscape.

gemini.depth_why: Scores dip during the rainy season and typhoon season due to clouds and ferry cancellations, peaking in midsummer.
gemini.overview: Okinawa is known for its dramatic coastlines and vivid blue waters. The primary draws are the sweeping ocean views along the Churaumi coast and the remote beaches of the Kerama Islands. Inland areas feature dense subtropical forests.

blurbs.text: Clear skies keep the coastal views sharp, with reliable ferry access to the outer islands and calm waters that reflect the sky.
The rainy season brings heavy cloud cover and frequent showers, dulling the bright colors of the ocean and coastlines.
Midsummer sun lights up the water, showing the vivid blues of the Kerama Islands and the Churaumi coast, though typhoons begin to reach the island this month.
Late summer brings a high risk of typhoons, which churn up the sea, bring heavy clouds, and frequently halt ferry access to the outer islands.
Typhoons still pass the island in October, and a storm can churn up the sea and halt ferries to the outer islands, though the skies clear and the water settles as the month goes on.

gemini.depth_why: Scores rise from winter closures to peak summer access, then fall as snow and rain return.
gemini.overview: Olympic National Park holds glaciated mountains, temperate rain forest and rugged Pacific coast. The Hoh Rain Forest has dense, moss-draped old growth, Rialto Beach has sea stacks and driftwood shores, and Hurricane Ridge looks across the Olympic Mountains to the Strait of Juan de Fuca.

blurbs.text: Rain and snow limit access. The Hurricane Ridge road is often closed or needs chains and many trails are snowbound, though the coast and lower rain forests stay reachable, wet and stormy.
Snow still blocks the high country, including Hurricane Ridge. The rain forests are lush from the winter rain and the coast is dramatic and moody.
Snow melts from the lower mountains and the Hurricane Ridge road usually opens for the season. Waterfalls run high and the rain forests are vibrant green.
Snow lingers only on the high country. Waterfalls still run strong, the rain forests are vibrant green and the Hurricane Ridge road is open.
The high country is clear of snow, opening the full range of mountain viewpoints and alpine trails, and the coast and rain forests are easy to reach in the driest weather of the year.
Heavy rain returns to the coast and forests, and early snow on the high mountain roads begins to limit access to the alpine viewpoints.

gemini.depth_why: Access to the high mountains and glaciers changes drastically with the snowpack, creating distinct seasons for road and trail access.
gemini.overview: Pakistan holds some of the highest mountain scenery on earth, anchored by the Karakoram and Himalayan ranges. Visitors travel the Karakoram Highway to see massive glaciers, deep river gorges, and the turquoise waters of Attabad Lake. The signature views include the Hunza Valley and the high-altitude pastures of Fairy Meadows sitting directly beneath the ice walls of Nanga Parbat.

blurbs.text: Heavy snow blocks the high mountain passes, including the route to Fairy Meadows and the Khunjerab Pass. Views in the lower valleys are snowbound, and many high-altitude roads become impassable.
Valleys like Hunza thaw into spring blossoms against the snowy mountain backdrops. High-altitude trails and major passes remain closed by snow, limiting access to the glaciers.

Warmer temperatures melt the lower snowpack, opening more roads and trails. The skies are generally clear before the summer heat, offering sharp views of the peaks, though the highest passes may still be blocked.

The high mountain roads, including Babusar Pass, are open, allowing access to the major glaciers and Fairy Meadows. The northern ranges sit in a rain shadow, keeping skies mostly clear of monsoon clouds for unobstructed views of Nanga Parbat.

Autumn turns the foliage in the northern valleys bright yellow and red. The skies remain clear for mountain viewing, but temperatures drop sharply and snow begins to threaten the high passes by the end of the month.
Winter sets in across the northern ranges, freezing the lakes and bringing heavy snow. The high passes close for the season, cutting off access to the upper glaciers and remote viewpoints.

gemini.depth_why: The Rock Islands stay the same, but the rains and rougher water affect the boat trips.
gemini.overview: Palau is known for its coastal scenery, particularly the Rock Islands, a maze of limestone formations covered in dense green foliage rising from clear turquoise lagoons. Visitors view these islands by boat, weaving through the channels, or from the air for a broader perspective of the reef systems.

blurbs.text: Calm seas and clear skies make the boat trips through the Rock Islands' narrow channels easy, with the limestone islets and the varied blues of the lagoons at their sharpest.
Showers and cloud come and go over the Rock Islands, and rougher water can limit some boat trips, though clear spells still show the turquoise lagoons and green limestone islets.

gemini.depth_why: Scores drop during the wet season when visibility and access to the islands are reduced.
gemini.overview: Palawan is known for its dramatic limestone karst islands rising from clear turquoise waters. The signature views are found by boat in El Nido's hidden lagoons and Coron's inland lakes. Inland, the island has dense tropical forests and modest waterfalls.

blurbs.text: The dry season provides the clearest skies and calmest waters for boat trips to the limestone karsts of El Nido and Coron. Visibility is excellent for taking in the dramatic coastal cliffs and hidden lagoons.

The transition to the wet season brings more frequent rain showers and increasing cloud cover. Boat trips to the lagoons and lakes still run, but the skies are often overcast, muting the colors of the water and cliffs.

Heavy rains and rougher seas are common during the wet season. Boat access to the signature coastal views in El Nido and Coron can be disrupted or canceled due to weather, and low clouds often obscure the limestone peaks.

The rains begin to ease, and the seas calm down as the dry season approaches. Access to the coastal karsts and lagoons becomes more reliable, though some lingering clouds and showers can still affect visibility.

gemini.depth_why: Scores fall into clear groups based on the dry and wet seasons, which dictate visibility and trail access.
gemini.overview: Panama is known for its tropical coastlines and dense rainforests. The San Blas islands provide classic white-sand and clear-water Caribbean scenery, while the capital offers the contrast of Casco Viejo's vibrant historic architecture against the modern city's skyline and the Pacific. Inland, the Chiriquí highlands hold lush cloud forest on the slopes of Volcán Barú.

blurbs.text: Clear skies make the coastal waters of the San Blas islands their brightest blue. Dry trails allow easier access to the highland cloud forests and volcano viewpoints.
Regular afternoon downpours are the norm. Cloud cover often obscures the mountain viewpoints, but the rainforests are a vibrant, lush green.
Heavy, persistent rains dominate. Coastal waters lose their clarity from runoff, and many unpaved highland trails become too muddy to navigate easily.
Rains taper off as the dry season approaches. The forests remain deeply green from the rains, and coastal skies begin to clear for better visibility.

gemini.depth_why: Scores rise during the dry season when the flooded plains recede and access improves, and fall during the wet season when heavy rains flood the region.
gemini.overview: The Pantanal is the world's largest tropical wetland, a vast expanse of flooded plains, winding rivers, and gallery forests. Boat trips give the best views of the intricate waterways and the reflections of the sky on the marshes. The landscape changes dramatically with the seasons, shifting from a flooded basin to drying lagoons and grassy plains.

blurbs.text: Heavy rains flood the basin, turning the landscape into a vast inland sea. Many dirt roads become impassable, limiting access to boat travel, but the high water creates striking reflections and allows boats to glide through flooded forests.
Floodwaters are still receding while the landscape stays lush and green, with water still covering much of the plains and keeping boat access open to the deeper channels and lagoons.

The dry season reveals the grassy plains as the water shrinks into isolated lagoons and river channels. Dirt roads are dry, allowing overland travel, and the remaining water concentrates the views around the shrinking pools and winding rivers.
The first rains of the wet season are filling the basin, and water levels are rising in the rivers and marshes. The landscape is moving back toward a flooded state.

gemini.depth_why: Scores rise during the drier months when trails and highland roads are more accessible, and fall during the wet season when heavy rains obscure views and wash out routes.
gemini.overview: Papua New Guinea is known for its rugged, densely forested highlands and remote coastal scenery. The Kokoda Track cuts through steep, jungle-clad mountains, while the coastal areas offer views of volcanic islands and coral reefs. The scenery is best seen during the drier months, when trails and highland roads are easier to navigate.

blurbs.text: Heavy rains define the wet season, swelling rivers and turning highland tracks into deep mud. Low clouds and frequent downpours often obscure the mountain views, and some remote roads become impassable.
The rains are easing and the dense forests are lush and vibrant. Trails like the Kokoda Track are drying out, making the steep valleys and mountain passes easier to reach.
The driest weather brings the clearest views of the rugged highlands and coastal islands. This is the most reliable time to hike the Kokoda Track or drive the highland roads without major washouts.
Humidity builds and afternoon showers are more frequent as the wet season approaches. The highland valleys remain green, but clouds gather around the peaks more often.

gemini.depth_why: The skyline stays the same, but winter is bare and gray and spring is in leaf and blossom.
gemini.overview: Paris presents an iconic urban landscape defined by the Seine and a historic skyline. The signature view is the Eiffel Tower rising above the river at dusk, best seen from the Trocadéro or the bridges. The dense layout provides sweeping panoramas from elevated points like Montmartre.

blurbs.text: Bare trees and gray skies mute the city, but the Seine and the zinc roofs still show well from Montmartre and the bridges, and the Eiffel Tower is lit at dusk.
Blossoms and fresh green leaves line the Seine, and long evenings show the Eiffel Tower and the zinc roofs from Montmartre and the Buttes-Chaumont.
Warm, long days frame the landmarks along the Seine, and Montmartre and the Buttes-Chaumont give wide views over the zinc roofs.

gemini.depth_why: Scores follow the dry and wet seasons, peaking in the clear winter months.
gemini.overview: The Andes define the region, anchored by the iconic mountain setting of Machu Picchu and the terraced slopes of the Sacred Valley. High-altitude trails and passes reveal snow-capped peaks, deep river gorges, and the mineral-striped slopes of Rainbow Mountain. The clearest views come in the dry months from May to September.

blurbs.text: Heavy rains bring low clouds that frequently obscure the peaks and valleys. Trails can be muddy, though the green, rain-washed terraces of the Sacred Valley are visible when the weather breaks.

Heavy rains bring low clouds that frequently obscure the peaks and valleys. The Inca Trail closes entirely this month for maintenance, though the green, rain-washed terraces of the Sacred Valley are visible when the weather breaks.
Rain and low clouds still hide the peaks and valleys much of the time. Trails can be muddy, though the green, rain-washed terraces of the Sacred Valley are visible when the weather breaks.
The rains begin to taper off, leaving the mountainsides bright green. Clouds still gather in the afternoons, but mornings often offer clear views of the peaks and the Urubamba River gorge.

Dry, clear days provide the sharpest views of the Andes. The skies over Machu Picchu and the high-altitude passes are typically blue, making this the most reliable time to see the snow-capped peaks and the vivid colors of Rainbow Mountain.
Clouds build and occasional showers soften the dry landscape. The high peaks are still visible, though afternoon fog can roll into the valleys.
Clouds and showers are frequent, and afternoon fog often rolls into the valleys and obscures the higher passes, though the high peaks show on clearer mornings.

gemini.depth_why: The year divides into a high-water wet season and a low-water dry season.
gemini.overview: The primary draw is the vast, unbroken expanse of the Amazon rainforest, best seen from the water. Riverboats navigate wide brown rivers and narrow tributaries, passing dark oxbow lakes and dense walls of green vegetation.

blurbs.text: High water floods the forest floor, so boats can follow channels through the flooded forest. Heavy rains are frequent and low clouds often hang over the rivers.

Receding waters reveal muddy riverbanks and clear the jungle trails for walking. The skies hold less rain, giving sharper views of the dense green canopy and the dark, still waters of the oxbow lakes.
