Golden larch forests add a new layer to the scenery. Lifts and huts close one by one, the Tre Cime toll road shuts as soon as snow or ice threatens, and even the main Val Gardena lifts stop running within days of the month's end. Early snow can close higher trails.
The summer lifts, mountain huts and the Tre Cime toll road are closed, and snow begins to close the high passes and trails, while the valleys are bare and cold before the ski lifts open.

gemini.depth_why: Scores rise from winter lows to a summer peak when ferries run and the caldera views are clearest.
gemini.overview: Santorini and the Cyclades are known for their dramatic coastal scenery and whitewashed villages built into steep cliffs. The signature view is the Santorini caldera, a flooded volcanic crater best seen from the towns of Oia and Fira. Beyond the famous sunsets, the islands offer rugged coastlines, volcanic beaches, and boat trips to the central volcano.

blurbs.text: Winter brings the wet season, with frequent rain and wind that can obscure the caldera views. Many ferries and boat tours to the volcano stop running, limiting access to the coastal scenery.
Spring weather brings clearer skies and better visibility of the cliffs and villages, and fuller ferry schedules make it easier to reach the viewpoints and volcanic beaches.
Clear skies give the best views of the famous Oia and Fira sunsets over the caldera. Boat trips to the volcano run frequently, and the coastal scenery is easy to reach.
October still provides good visibility for the caldera and coastal views, though the chance of rain increases late in the month. Most boat tours and ferries continue to operate.

gemini.depth_why: Scores drop in the wet winter months when visibility and access can be affected by rain and high water.
gemini.overview: Venice's scenery is defined by its canals, lagoons, and historic architecture. The signature views are the Grand Canal and St. Mark's Square, where the water meets the city. Beyond the main islands, the Venetian Lagoon offers views of marshlands and smaller islands like Murano and Burano. The best time to see the city and lagoon is during the drier months from spring through autumn.

blurbs.text: High water (acqua alta) often floods low-lying areas such as St. Mark's Square, and fog is common, reducing visibility across the lagoon and along the canals.

Drier weather and clearer skies make this the best time to view the Grand Canal and explore the wider Venetian Lagoon. The light is better for seeing the contrast between the water and the city's architecture.

gemini.depth_why: Scores reflect the seasonal access to ferries, trails, and coastal views, peaking in summer and dropping in winter when services are reduced.
gemini.overview: The Amalfi Coast is known for its dramatic meeting of steep mountains and the Tyrrhenian Sea, creating one of the world's most famous coastal landscapes. Villages like Positano cling to the cliffs, offering iconic views of pastel houses stacked above the water. The scenery is best seen from the water on a boat trip or from high above on the Path of the Gods hiking trail.

blurbs.text: The coast is quiet and some ferries have stopped running, making it harder to view the cliffs from the water. Rain can make the steep hiking trails muddy.

The coast is quiet and access to the scenery is limited. Many ferries stop running, making it harder to view the cliffs from the water, and winter rains can make the steep hiking trails muddy or unsafe.
Skies are clearer and ferries run, opening up views of the coastline from the water, though rain is still occasional. The Path of the Gods and other trails are accessible and green.
Skies are clear and ferries run, opening up views of the coastline from the water. The Path of the Gods and other trails are accessible and green.

The coastal views are at their best, with full ferry schedules allowing easy access to the water for looking back at the cliffs and villages. The Path of the Gods offers clear, sweeping views over the sea, though the trails and viewpoints are busy.

The dramatic coastal views remain clear, and ferries still run frequently enough to see the cliffs from the water. The Path of the Gods is open and less crowded than in summer, though late October brings a higher chance of rain.

gemini.depth_why: Scores change as the North Rim opens and closes, and summer monsoons affect visibility.
gemini.overview: The Grand Canyon is known for its massive scale, exposing layered red and orange rock walls that drop thousands of feet to the Colorado River. The South Rim provides the most famous vantage points, especially at sunrise and sunset when the light shifts across the canyon floor. Visitors can hike down the Bright Angel and South Kaibab trails for a closer look at the geology, or take a helicopter flight for views from the air.

blurbs.text: Snow often coats the upper ledges of the South Rim, adding white contrast to the red rock. The North Rim is closed for the winter, and some trails may be icy, but clear days offer sharp visibility.
Warmer temperatures melt the winter snow on the South Rim, making the Bright Angel and South Kaibab trails easier to hike. The North Rim stays closed, but the main viewpoints are open.
The North Rim opens in mid-May, adding access to the far side of the canyon. Skies are generally clear, providing unobstructed views across the vast expanse from every overlook.
Both rims are open and skies are generally clear, providing unobstructed views across the vast expanse from every overlook.

Summer brings the monsoon season, with sudden afternoon thunderstorms rolling across the canyon. These storms can briefly hide the views behind rain and clouds, but they also create dramatic lighting and occasional rainbows.
The monsoon storms fade early in the month, leaving crisp air and excellent visibility for looking deep into the canyon. Both rims are open.
Crisp air and excellent visibility make for long views into the canyon, and the Kaibab Plateau shows patches of fall color. The North Rim stays open until mid-October.
The North Rim is closed for the season, leaving the South Rim as the primary vantage point. Early snowstorms can occasionally obscure the canyon, but most days remain clear and cool.

gemini.depth_why: Scores rise and fall with daylight and access to the interior.
gemini.overview: Iceland is known for its dramatic geology, with massive glaciers, black sand beaches, and some of the most powerful waterfalls in the world. The landscape is largely treeless and volcanic, shaped by ice and fire into deep canyons, geothermal valleys, and jagged coastlines. The best time to see the scenery is summer, when the highland roads open and long daylight hours allow for extended drives.

blurbs.text: Short daylight hours limit how much can be seen in a day, and snow often blankets the landscape, adding a white backdrop to the waterfalls and black sand beaches. The highland roads to places like Landmannalaugar are closed, but coastal routes and major waterfalls like Skógafoss are still open.

Daylight increases rapidly, revealing the transition from winter to spring. Snow still blankets much of the country, adding to the winter scenery, and while the interior highlands remain closed to regular traffic, the coastal ring road offers clear views of the glaciers and fjords.
The snow melts from the lowlands, and the days grow very long. The waterfalls run high with meltwater, though the highland roads typically remain closed until later in the season.

The midnight sun provides nearly endless daylight for driving and hiking. The mountain roads open, allowing access to the colorful rhyolite peaks of Landmannalaugar and the deep interior, while the Jökulsárlón glacier lagoon is open.
Autumn colors show in the low brush, with the first dustings of snow on the peaks. Daylight has settled at ordinary lengths, and the highland roads are usually still open.
Fresh snow dusts the peaks, though the highland roads usually close this month as winter weather sets in. The coastal routes and big waterfalls such as Skógafoss are still open.

gemini.depth_why: Scores rise slightly in the drier, clearer winter months.
gemini.overview: Rio de Janeiro is known for its dramatic setting, where steep granite peaks rise directly from the Atlantic Ocean. The city is built around these mountains and bays, creating a famous skyline visible from the beaches of Ipanema and Copacabana. The Tijuca Forest covers the higher slopes, offering viewpoints like the summit of Corcovado and Sugarloaf Mountain.

blurbs.text: Heavy rain and frequent cloud cover can obscure the higher peaks. The views from the beaches remain clear, but the summits of Corcovado and Sugarloaf are often wrapped in mist.
The heavy rains ease, leaving clearer skies and better visibility for the mountain viewpoints. The forests on the slopes are lush from the wet season.
Dry weather gives the most reliable visibility for the city's signature views. Clear skies make this the best time to see the coastline from the summits of Corcovado and Sugarloaf.
Rain and cloud cover are on the rise, so visibility from the higher viewpoints is less predictable, though the coastal scenery remains striking.

gemini.depth_why: Scores reflect the shift between peak summer access, snowy winter views, and the transitional shoulder seasons.
gemini.overview: The Swiss Alps offer some of the most famous mountain scenery in the world, anchored by the jagged profile of the Matterhorn above Zermatt. Visitors ride the Glacier Express past deep valleys and high peaks, or view the sheer cliffs and plunging waterfalls of Lauterbrunnen. Glaciers, alpine lakes, and traditional timber villages complete the landscape.

blurbs.text: Thick snow covers the valleys and peaks, turning the region into a brilliant white landscape. High mountain passes are closed to drivers, but cable cars and winter trains provide access to high-altitude viewpoints.
Snow begins to retreat from the lower valleys, though the high peaks remain heavily blanketed and most high passes stay closed.
Melting snow brings heavy flow to the waterfalls in Lauterbrunnen. Many high hiking trails and driving passes remain blocked by snowpack.
The valleys are bright green and the high mountain passes are fully open for driving and hiking. Glaciers and alpine lakes are accessible, and clear days offer sharp views of the Matterhorn.
Autumn brings yellow and orange tones to the lower forests. High passes begin to close as the first snows arrive at elevation.
The landscape transitions to winter, with gray skies and early snow accumulating in the valleys before the winter season fully begins.

gemini.depth_why: The scenery in Barcelona is primarily urban and coastal, which remains visible and accessible throughout the year.
gemini.overview: Barcelona is known for its urban landscape and Mediterranean coastline. The most famous views are of Antoni Gaudí's architecture, particularly the Sagrada Família and the city panorama from Park Güell. Beaches line the coast, with the Collserola hills as a backdrop.

blurbs.text: The panoramas from Park Güell and the Collserola hills show the grid of the Eixample district and the Mediterranean Sea beyond.

gemini.depth_why: The river and the painted streets stay the same, but heat, gray days and the jacaranda bloom change how they look.
gemini.overview: The primary views in the Argentine capital come from its setting along the wide Río de la Plata. Visitors stroll the brightly painted houses of the La Boca neighborhood and the tree-lined avenues of Recoleta.

blurbs.text: Heat and humidity make it hard to linger along the river, and the Caminito in La Boca and the shaded streets of Recoleta are best seen in the early morning.
Mild to cool, often gray days mute the Río de la Plata, but the painted facades of the Caminito in La Boca and the shaded streets of Recoleta keep their color.
Mild, clearer days brighten the painted facades of the Caminito in La Boca and the shaded streets of Recoleta.
Jacaranda trees bloom purple along the streets, adding color to the shaded avenues of Recoleta and the painted facades of the Caminito in La Boca.
